summary: Mark Allon is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned an Honours degree from Australian National University and a PhD from Cambridge under Kenneth Roy Norman (~1989–1994), later holding posts at SOAS (~1994–2000) and Sydney (~2002).

Mark C. Elliott is a scholar in Sinology, Inner Asian history, and archaeology. He has served as a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and as Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi works in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2003–2006) and became Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at the University of California, Berkeley around 2005.

Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Exeter (1987–1990). He held a post at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) before joining Nottingham Trent University in 1995, where he became Professor of Gambling Studies around 1995.

Mark Juergensmeyer works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Illinois (~1958–1962), Union Theological Seminary (~1962–1965), and Columbia University, later becoming professor of sociology and religious studies at UC Santa Barbara (~1989).

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held an assistant professorship at the State University of New York (attested 2005) and served as an associate professor at University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2006).
Mark Owen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Leeds under the supervision of Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski was an Indologist who completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford (~1975–1980) under Richard Gombrich. He also studied under traditional teachers Lakshman Joo (~1970–1991) and Kedar Raj Rajopadhyaya.

Mark Siderits works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Illinois State University (~1979–2008; Emeritus Professor attested 2007–2014) and served as Emeritus Professor of Philosophy at Seoul National University (attested 2011–2014).

Mark Singleton is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed a PhD at the University of Cambridge, studied under teacher Lakshmi Tatacharya, and served as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

Mark T. Unno specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin College (~1977–1981) and Stanford University (~1988–1994), later holding posts at Brown University (~1994–1998) and the University of Oregon (~1998).

Mark Tatz was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (1978). He also studied under several traditional teachers and taught at CIIS (attested 1988).

Mark Teeuwen specializes in Japanology and religious studies. After completing his Ph.D. at Leiden University (~1990–1996), he was appointed Professor of Japanese Studies at the University of Oslo around 1999.

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Vienna (-2012) under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, later working there (attested 2011) and as a project researcher at Heidelberg University.

Marsha Weidner is a scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, she held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at New York University (~1966–1969) and Harvard (~1969–1975). She held posts at Harvard (~1975–1983), Brown University (~1984–1995), and the University of Chicago (~1995).
Martin Baumann is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He took up a post at the University of Lucerne in 2001, where he served as Professor of Religious Studies.

Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at the University of Zurich (~1969–1979) and Delhi (~1971–1972), alongside numerous traditional teachers. He served as Konservator at the University of Zurich (~1975–2008).

Martin Collcutt studied at Cambridge and Harvard. He taught at Yokohama National University and the University of Tokyo (1963–1969), and served as a professor and Director of the East Asian Studies Program at Princeton University (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto and Hamburg (-2002, PhD). He has held positions at Göttingen, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, Ryukoku University, Hamburg (2011), and Shandong University (2019).
